bib.title: Rethinking Mixture-of-Agents: Is Mixing Different Large Language Models Beneficial?

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Rethinking Mixture-of-Agents: Is Mixing Different Large Language Models Beneficial?" (Self-MoA), Wenzhe Li*, Yong Lin*, Mengzhou Xia, Chi Jin, Princeton. arXiv 2502.00674v1, 2 Feb 2025, preprint. Title verified on page 1.
COVERAGE: all 22 pages read, 57385 chars, including appendices A-B and tables 8-12. References skimmed. Extraction clean. Figure 2/3 plot data are not in the text.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Self-MoA (sample one top model N times, then aggregate) beats a standard mixed-model 2-layer MoA on AlpacaEval 2.0.
  number: 65.7 vs 59.1 LC win rate (+6.6)
  setup: six open models as in Wang et al. 2024a. Self-MoA uses 6 samples of WizardLM-2-8x22B. Aggregator Qwen1.5-110B-Chat for both. Temp 0.7. AlpacaEval 2.0 LC win rate. WizardLM alone scores 53.1.
  quote: "Self-MoA demonstrates remarkable effectiveness in this task, outperforming the Mixed-MoA baseline by 6.6 point." Table 1: "Mixed-MoA 2-Layer MoA [Wang et al., 2024a] 59.1 ... Self-MoA 2-Layer Self-MoA + WizardLM 65.7"
  where: p.5
- With task-specialised 7B models, Self-MoA using the best model per task beats all 13 mixed configurations on every task.
  number: MMLU 69.01, CRUX 50.75, MATH 68.42 (Self-MoA, aggregator i) vs Mixed-MoA best per task of 68.90, 47.00, 67.62. Average gain is 3.8%.
  setup: Qwen2-7B-Instruct (i), DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite (d), Qwen2-Math-7B (m). 6 proposers. Aggregator mainly Qwen2-7B, temp 0 for aggregator, 0.7 for proposers. MMLU-redux 3,000 samples, CRUX 800, MATH test 5,000.
  quote: "When using i as the aggregator, Self-MoA with the TaskBest model consistently outperforms all 13 tested Mixed-MoA configurations across all tasks." Also "adopting a task-specific aggregator yields an additional performance boost of 1-2 points."
  where: p.7 (Table 3)
- MoA performance depends on both proposer quality and diversity, but is more sensitive to quality.
  number: regression coefficients quality α vs diversity β: MMLU 2.558 vs 1.841, CRUX 4.548 vs 1.421, MATH 4.719 vs 2.839. R² 0.771, 0.685, 0.760. All p<0.001.
  setup: about 70 proposer mixtures per dataset (model combinations, temps 0.5 to 1.2). Diversity is the Vendi Score. Quality is the mean proposer accuracy. Both normalised.
  quote: "α is greater than β across all three datasets... MoA's performance is particularly sensitive to variations in quality" Table 4: "MMLU 2.558 ± 0.176 ... 1.841 ± 0.176 ... 0.771"
  where: pp.9-10
- Better quality measures raise the fit.
  number: R² above 0.9 on MMLU with Centered-1/K-Norm, K=2 to 4 (0.881, 0.902, 0.903)
  setup: weights the best proposers more. Not consistent on MATH because the Qwen2-7B aggregator is weak at math.
  quote: "on MMLU... the R2 value can exceed 0.9 with K = 2 using the Centered-1/K-Norm."
  where: pp.10-11 (Table 5)
- Mixing models helps only when the models are of similar quality and differ in strengths (mixed-skill task). Even then the margin is tiny.
  number: Mixed mmmddd 60.04 and mmdddd 59.86 vs Self-MoA dddddd 59.69 (+0.35 and +0.17). Self-MoA with TaskBest, which needs prior knowledge of the task, gets 62.73 (aggregator i) and 63.81 (aggregator TaskBest).
  setup: mixture task with samples drawn uniformly from MMLU, CRUX and MATH, source unknown to the models. Average of the three.
  quote: "Mixed-MoA of mmdddd and mmmddd achieves the average performance of 59.86% and 60.04%, improves upon Self-MoA of dddddd by 0.17% and 0.35%."
  where: pp.11-12 (Table 6)
- Self-MoA beats Mixed-MoA even when two models have similar individual accuracy.
  number: MMLU 71.27 (llllll) vs 70.73 (iiilll) vs 69.01 (iiiiii). Individual i 66.16, l 66.40.
  setup: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct vs Qwen2-7B-Instruct, aggregator Qwen2-7B.
  quote: Table 7: "Self-MoA i iiiiii 69.01 i llllll 71.27" and "Mixed-MoA i iiilll 70.73"
  where: p.12
- Self-MoA lifts the top AlpacaEval 2.0 models, with a new leaderboard first at submission.
  number: gemma-2-9b-it-WPO-HB 76.7 to 78.5. gemma-2-9b-it-SimPO 72.4 to 75.0.
  setup: each model is both proposer and aggregator. Only 4 outputs because of the Gemma 2 context limit (8192 tokens). Temp 0.7.
  quote: "Self-MoA consistently achieves a 2-3 point gain and secures the top position on the leaderboard during submission."
  where: p.6 (Table 2)
- Self-MoA is cheaper than deeper mixed MoA at equal quality.
  number: 3-layer Mixed-MoA 65.4 LC with 13 forward passes vs 2-layer Self-MoA 65.7 with 7. MT-Bench: Self-MoA 9.13 vs 2-layer MoA 9.06 (7 passes each). With GPT-4o aggregator, Self-MoA 9.52 (7 passes) vs 3-layer MoA 9.40 (13 passes).
  setup: WizardLM-2-8x22B proposer, Qwen1.5-110B aggregator (AlpacaEval). The 3-layer MoA and MT-Bench numbers for 3-layer MoA are copied from Wang et al.
  quote: "Self-MoA outperforms the 3-layer Mixed-MoA baseline with only half the forward passes." Table 8: "65.4 13 ... 65.7 7"
  where: p.19, p.21
- Self-MoA also beats Universal Self-Consistency (pick the most consistent output) at the same compute.
  number: AlpacaEval LC: Self-MoA 65.7 vs Self-USC 60.2. Mixed-MoA 59.1 vs Mixed-USC 53.8. All use 7 forward passes.
  setup: same as Table 1.
  quote: "USC performs worse than its MoA counterpart when proposers and aggregators are controlled."
  where: p.20-22 (Table 12)
- Self-MoA-Seq (sliding-window aggregation) matches or slightly beats one-shot Self-MoA, so it works beyond the aggregator's context limit.
  number: samples varied 6 to 30. The text gives no table values. Adding Llama-3.1-8B after 30 Qwen2 samples gave about +2%. Adding DeepSeek-Coder, which is 5% weaker, gave a drop of more than 1.5%.
  setup: MMLU (Qwen2-7B) and CRUX (DeepSeek-Coder), temp 0.7, window size 6 with 3 slots reserved for the current synthesis, 3 seeds.
  quote: "Self-MoA-Seq delivers performance that is comparable to, or slightly better than, Self-MoA." "adding DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct reduces accuracy by more than 1.5%."
  where: p.13
- More samples do not reliably help.
  number: none
  quote: "Adding more samples can have both positive and negative effects, meaning there is no universal compute-optimal solution."
  where: p.13
- Cross-model diversity in the same-quality case: mixing a similar-quality second model helped (+2%), a weaker one hurt.
  number: see above
  where: p.13

LIMITS
- Models are small, open and old (2024): 7B-8B models for Tables 3 to 7, Qwen1.5/WizardLM for AlpacaEval. No frontier models, apart from GPT-4o as aggregator in MT-Bench.
- Self-MoA assumes you know which single model is best. The TaskBest wins need prior knowledge of the task, which the authors concede for the mixed task (Table 6).
- The authors could not reproduce Wang et al.'s single-proposer result and conjecture that the proposer choice (not stated in Wang) explains it (footnote p.5).
- Diversity of samples from one model plateaus. Aggregating many samples is harder, and context length caps the count (p.12). Scaling is not monotone.
- Regression is correlational. Quality is task accuracy, and the diversity metric is the Vendi Score.
- Some points use a reduced proposer length and 3 outputs because Qwen2-Math is limited to a 4096 context (footnote p.6).
- Only the aggregation topology (parallel proposers, one aggregator, optional extra layers) is tested. No dependent or adaptive topologies.

BUILDS ON
- Mixture-of-Agents, Wang et al. 2024a (the prompt pipeline and the six-model setup).
- Repeated sampling and test-time scaling: Brown et al. 2024 (Large Language Monkeys), Snell et al. 2024.
- Self-consistency (Wang et al. 2022) and Universal Self-Consistency (Chen et al. 2023b); best-of-n (Gui et al. 2024); More Agents Is All You Need (Li et al. 2024).
- Ensembling: LLM-Blender (Jiang et al. 2023a); MoA in SWE (Zhang et al. 2024b); the OpenPipe 2024 blog.
- Multi-agent debate (Du et al. 2023; Liang et al. 2023; RECONCILE, Chen et al. 2023a); Self-Refine (Madaan et al. 2024).
- Wang et al. 2024b: a single prompted model can match agent discussion.
- Vendi Score (Friedman and Dieng 2023).
- Benchmarks: AlpacaEval 2.0 (Dubois et al. 2024), MMLU-redux, CRUXEval, MATH, MT-Bench.

CODE: none in the PDF. The multi-layer MoA formula is in A.1 (p.19). Vendi Score: VS(K) = exp(-sum λ_i log λ_i) over the eigenvalues of K/n (p.19).

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.4): MoA (several models, one aggregator) vs Self-MoA (one model sampled repeatedly, one aggregator) vs Self-MoA-Seq (sliding window, with the current best output repeated to bias the aggregator). Shows the topology differences at a glance.
- Fig 2 (p.8): scatter of quality vs diversity, coloured by performance, for MMLU, CRUX and MATH. Best results sit at high quality and lower diversity. The trade-off Pareto front is visible.
- Fig 3 (p.13): accuracy vs number of samples (6 to 30) for Self-MoA and Self-MoA-Seq on MMLU and CRUX.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions. Table 2 and Table 7 columns are slightly run together in the extraction, but the values are readable. Table 5 for MATH shows K-Norm and Centered rows identical, as printed. The text conflates "2-3 point gain" for Table 2 (actual gains 1.8 and 2.6).
